name: gnu-barcode
desc: Convert text strings to printed bars
why: Turns text into printed barcode bars, a small transform with a retro charm but limited depth.

brief.what_it_is: GNU Barcode is a command-line tool and library that converts text strings into printed barcode bars. It takes a text string and a chosen encoding standard, and outputs PostScript or Encapsulated PostScript. The homepage says it supports UPC, EAN, ISBN, CODE39 and other standards. It can also produce tables of barcodes laid out for sticker label sheets.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives no explicit motivation. It presents the tool as a way to turn text into printable barcodes in standard encodings, with output sized in inches, centimeters or millimeters.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. It says the program creates PostScript output, that sizes and positions can be given in inches, centimeters or millimeters, and that it can lay out tables of barcodes for label sheets. It is available both as a library and as an executable.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps beyond download sources. Source is available from the main GNU download server over HTTP(S) and FTP, and from GNU mirrors, which the page asks users to prefer. The Homebrew entry lists two executables, barcode and sample. The page mentions no runtime, account or configuration needs.
brief.standout: It is a small, old-school GNU utility that emits PostScript rather than PNG or SVG, so the output drops straight into print workflows. It also does label-sheet tables, which many simple barcode generators skip.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage's last-updated stamp reads 2020/08/04 and the page shows copyright years up to 2009. No release version or recent commit date appeared on the page, so current activity cannot be confirmed from this page alone.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not list the full set of supported encodings or give usage examples. Output is PostScript, so a viewer or converter is needed for PNG or PDF. The Homebrew scout notes describe it as having limited depth. The fetch covered only the homepage, so the manual and release history are unchecked.
